reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows L1₀ ordering and high anisotropy only at 50 at.% Pt in a different alloy (FeCoNiMnCu), not at the proposed 10-15 at.% in FeCoNi. No evidence supports partial ordering at low Pt levels, the specific coercivity increase, or the maintenance of high-entropy status under these conditions. The conflicting evidence (E3) is unrelated to the hypothesis.
premises: Minor Pt doping (~10-15 at.%) in FeCoNi can induce partial L1₀-type ordering.
Partial L1₀ ordering increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain wall pinning.
Increased anisotropy and pinning raise coercivity by an order of magnitude over undoped FeCoNi.
The alloy remains a high-entropy alloy (configurational entropy ≥1.0R) with this Pt content.
Rapid thermal annealing (e.g., 350°C/30s) is sufficient to develop the ordered regions.
